article.title: NFL EDGE Wednesday Morning Brief
article.dek: The board flipped to Week 11 overnight with two cards and no Value play, Thursday's teams are banged up, and the betting splits still show the public and the money on opposite sides of the big Thursday spread.

items.headline: The board flipped to Week 11 overnight — and there is no Value card
paragraphs: Week 11 opens Thursday night with the Indianapolis Colts at the Houston Texans, 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff at NRG Stadium.

The app's board flipped overnight. Thirteen games are priced, and there are two cards on it. Hit Rate is the Bengals moneyline at -295 on FanDuel for Monday night. Balanced is the Vikings +3 at +100 on FanDuel for Sunday night.
The Value card is empty. The app found no +EV price on the board this week, and it says so plainly instead of forcing one.
items.takeaway: Two cards, no Value card. Hit Rate is Bengals moneyline -295, Balanced is Vikings +3 at +100, and nothing on the board is +EV this week.

items.headline: Injury news: Thursday's teams are banged up, and two Sunday quarterbacks are in doubt
paragraphs: For Thursday, Houston is missing pieces on both sides of the ball. Danielle Hunter and Marvin Harrison Jr. did not practice Monday or Tuesday, and Woody Marks is doubtful with a concussion. David Montgomery was a full participant and is trending to return.

The Colts' top two corners, Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, missed both walkthroughs and are trending out. Left tackle Bernhard Raimann missed both walkthroughs with a concussion, and Jalen Travis is doubtful. Daniel Jones is confirmed as Indy's starter.

For Sunday, Baker Mayfield is questionable with a foot strain and the reporting says he is trending toward missing the game at Detroit. Jalon Daniels would start if he sits. The app still lists Mayfield as Tampa Bay's expected starter, so trust the reporting here, not the app, and watch Wednesday's practice.

Geno Smith is questionable with an ankle injury, but the Jets say he starts at the Chargers if he is healthy. The app lists him as the expected starter. Drake Maye is likely done for the year with a fractured ankle, and the Patriots are on bye.
items.takeaway: Thursday's final designations come after Wednesday's practice, and inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff. Mayfield is the one to watch: the app still shows him starting, but the reporting says he is trending to miss Sunday.

items.headline: Weather: mild everywhere, and Thursday is under a roof
paragraphs: Thursday in Houston is about 68 degrees with light wind and a low rain chance, and there is a roof over the field anyway.

Sunday's outdoor games are mild too. Buffalo is about 60 degrees with a chance of rain showers and wind gusting into the 20s. Chicago is about 49 degrees and mostly sunny with a breeze. Denver is about 48 degrees, mostly sunny, and calm.
No game this week has real weather trouble. Nothing here changes how a game should be priced.
items.takeaway: Weather is a non-factor this week: mild everywhere, Thursday under a roof, and no outdoor game with wind trouble.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Two cards, no Value card — here is how to read them
paragraphs: Hit Rate is the pick most likely to win. The Bengals moneyline at -295 is the app's strongest win-probability play: the app puts Cincinnati at about 74% to win, against a market price that needs about 75% to break even. That is fine. Hit Rate forgoes value for win probability, and the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.
Balanced is the middle ground. The Vikings +3 at +100 is a good starting point: about a coin flip by the app's numbers, at even money.
Value is always the app's +EV play. This week there is not one. An empty Value card is the app being honest, not broken. Do not go hunting for a third card that is not there.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate is Bengals moneyline -295: the most likely winner, not a value play. Balanced is Vikings +3 at +100. Value is empty because nothing on the board is +EV.

items.headline: The app thinks the big spreads are too fat — and it still did not bet any of them
paragraphs: Look at the gaps. The app has Kansas City by about 6 points; the market has the Chiefs -16.5. It has Buffalo by about 3; the market has the Bills -16.5. It has Houston by less than a point; the market has the Texans -12.5. It has Chicago by a fraction of a point; the market has the Bears -11.5.

That is a real disagreement. But none of those underdogs made the board as a card. A gap is a question, not a pick. The app only posts a card when the whole check passes, and this week only two plays passed.

If your book has a better number than the app's board on one of these dogs, that is what Check is for. Type in your book's line and price and let the app run it back through the model and give you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: The app's margins are far under the market on all four double-digit favorites, but none of those dogs cleared the bar for a card. A gap alone is not a bet — run your price through Check.

items.headline: Two Sunday games the app cannot price yet
paragraphs: Jaguars at Giants and Steelers at Eagles have no market observations in the app. The books have not fed the app lines for those two games yet.

That does not mean there is nothing there. It means the app cannot price them until the lines land. Your book already has them. Type your book's line into Check and the app will give you a verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Jaguars at Giants and Steelers at Eagles are unpriced in the app. Use Check with your book's line until the board catches up.

items.headline: The public is on the Colts. The money is still on the Texans.
paragraphs: We checked the splits this morning. On the spread, 62% of the bets are on the Colts +12.5, but only 40% of the money is. The Texans -12.5 have 38% of the bets and 60% of the money.
That is the same split we saw Tuesday evening, and it held overnight. The money moved 7 points toward the Colts since then, but most tickets are still on one side and most money on the other.

The line backs it up. DraftKings still shows Texans -12.5, and Pinnacle has moved to -13. The total and the moneyline show no split at all: the over has 69% of the money and 66% of the bets, and the Texans moneyline is 90% on both counts.

Here is how to use it. If the public keeps hammering the Colts and the dog's price gets better without any new bad Texans news, you may be looking at the same football opinion for a better price. Watch whether DraftKings follows Pinnacle to -13. And run either side through Check at your price before you decide anything.
This is decision context, not a pick. The Fade does not override the app.
items.takeaway: Most bets are on the Colts, most money is on the Texans, and the line nudged toward Houston at Pinnacle. Use it as context, not a pick — and run your side through Check at your price.

items.headline: Houston keeps getting more expensive
paragraphs: The Texans opened -10 at DraftKings. They are -12.5 there now, unchanged overnight, and Pinnacle has them at -13. The total has not moved from 44.5 at DraftKings or FanDuel.
The Colts moneyline is +525 at DraftKings and +540 at FanDuel. The books keep lengthening the Colts' price while the Texans' spread grows.
Monday night is the closest big game to the app's numbers: the Bengals are -6.5 at DraftKings and the app has them by about 5. Every other double-digit favorite is far from the app's margin.
If your book still shows Texans -12.5 and Check says bet, bet now. Waiting risks -13 becoming the number everywhere, and a good number today beats a hoped-for number tomorrow.
items.takeaway: Texans -10 to -12.5 at DraftKings, now -13 at Pinnacle. Total steady at 44.5. If your book still has -12.5 and Check says bet, take it now.

items.headline: Thursday game? Thursday check.
paragraphs: Inactives land about 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff on Thursday. That is when you will know for sure about Gardner, Ward, Hunter, and Harrison Jr.
Line up your Thursday number now. Run it through Check at your book's price, and let the app give you a verdict. The board refreshes every morning and evening, so check again when it turns.
And do not force anything on the two games the app cannot price yet. Check them with your book's line, or leave them alone until the board catches up.
items.takeaway: Thursday game, Thursday check: inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff, so line up your number now and run it through Check at your price.
